caption: The drawing consists of a large rectangular textile design rendered primarily in red on a cream or off-white background. The central motif of the textile features a symmetrical arrangement of floral patterns and rosettes, surrounded by stylized leaves and vines. Four prominent eagles, each with wings spread and a shield on their chest, are placed around the central pattern. Scattered stars and stylized leaf shapes fill the background space. In the lower left corner, there is a depiction of a mounted figure pointing outward, with the text "1841" and the phrase "UNITED WE STAND DIVIDED WE FALL" next to it. Below this, a rectangular border contains the words "WASHINGTON" and "UNDER THIS WE PROSPER," along with the name "J. CUNNINGHAM WEAVER N. HARTFORD ONEIDA C. N. YORK." In the upper right corner of the drawing, there is a smaller inset that shows a reduced version of the textile’s complete design, bordered by a frame. The overall composition is highly geometric, repeating, and symmetrical in its layout, employing only red coloration for the decorative elements and inscriptions against the plain background.
title: Handwoven Coverlet
cluster: #22 — Domestic Textiles: Coverlets, Tablecloths, and Rugs
